result: The authors determined the cryo-EM structure of the H. pylori Cag T4SS, revealing a mushroom-shaped complex (~410 Å × ~460 Å) with three major regions: a 14-fold symmetric OMCC, a 17-fold symmetric PRC, and a central stalk. High-resolution maps (3.7 Å for OMCC, 3.5 Å for PRC) enabled secondary structure tracing, revealing an unexpected symmetry mismatch between the OMCC and PRC.
evaluation: Claims C12-C22 collectively describe the overall structure determination with appropriate resolution metrics and structural features. The symmetry assignments (C13, C14), resolution values (C19-C21), and structural organization (C12, C17) are internally consistent and supported by the cryo-EM data shown in Figures 1-2. The symmetry mismatch (C15) is a direct observation from the data.

result: The purified Cag T4SS structure closely matches the Cag T4SS detected in intact H. pylori by cryo-electron tomography.
evaluation: Claim C18 is supported by visual comparison in Figure 1B and citations to prior cryo-ET studies (Chang et al., 2018; Hu et al., 2019). The structural features appear consistent between the purified complex and in situ observations, validating that the purification did not significantly alter the structure.

result: The Stalk region could not be resolved at high resolution due to limited particle numbers, though low-resolution density suggests a possible channel through this region.
evaluation: Claims C23-C24 and C29 clearly state the limitation in resolving the Stalk. Claim C28 appropriately qualifies the channel observation as suggestive rather than definitive. This is an honest assessment of data limitations and appropriately cautious interpretation.

result: A large cavity runs through the Cag T4SS from the OMCC through the PRC, with the Stalk extending from the PRC through the inner membrane. Prior cryo-ET studies of H. pylori and L. pneumophila T4SSs proposed a channel in the Stalk region.
evaluation: Claims C25-C26 describe directly observable features in the structure (Figure 1E,F). Claim C27 appropriately cites prior work supporting the channel hypothesis. The cavity through OMCC and PRC is clearly visible in the presented maps.

result: The OMCC has a distinctive architecture with central and outer rings connected by spokes, organized into O-layer and I-layer. The spokes and outer rings are present in both layers of the Cag T4SS but absent in minimized T4SSs.
evaluation: Claims C30-C33 describe structural features directly observable in Figures 2-3. The measurements (C31) are consistent with the scale bars shown. Claim C34 makes a comparative statement that is reasonable based on known structures of minimized T4SSs, though direct side-by-side comparison is limited.

result: Portions of CagY, CagX, and CagT were traced and identified in the OMCC. CagY forms the cap crest with helices predicted to breach the outer membrane. CagX has a long helix extending through the OMCC layers. CagT has a globular subdomain and helical extension contributing to the spokes.
evaluation: Claims C36-C42 describe specific structural features visible in the high-resolution maps (Figure 4). The residue ranges traced (C36) are specific and verifiable. Claim C38 appropriately qualifies the membrane-breaching as a prediction. Claims C43-C44 acknowledge a predicted lipidation site not observed but note positioning consistent with membrane interaction. The level of detail is appropriate for the resolution achieved.

result: Unidentified protein components were modeled as polyalanine chains in the O-layer and I-layer. Cag3 is predicted to be in the OMCC periphery based on prior deletion studies. The I-layer is predicted to contain portions of CagY and CagX, but unambiguous assignment was not possible.
evaluation: Claims C45-C46 and C48 honestly acknowledge regions where protein identity could not be determined despite traceable density. Claims C47 and C49 appropriately cite prior work to support predictions while acknowledging the inability to obtain definitive assignments. This represents appropriate scientific caution when data quality limits interpretation.

result: The PRC is a hollow tube (90 Å × 185 Å, 96 Å internal diameter) with 17-fold symmetry connecting the OMCC and Stalk. Three polyalanine chains were modeled but could not be unambiguously assigned to CagM or other components. PRCs were not detected in E. coli or X. citri T4SSs but were identified in H. pylori and L. pneumophila cryo-ET studies.
evaluation: Claims C50-C51 provide specific measurements from the structure (Figure 4D-E). Claims C52-C53 appropriately cite prior literature for comparative context. Claims C54-C56 acknowledge the limitation in protein assignment while describing what could be modeled. The comparative analysis with other T4SSs is well-supported by citations.

result: A symmetry mismatch exists between the 14-fold OMCC and 17-fold PRC. In the lower-resolution C1 structure, physical contacts are visible, but these connections are lost in refined symmetric structures. The connection may involve contacts between 14 CagX helices and 17 PRC helices, with flexible helix tips.
evaluation: Claim C57 describes a key structural observation directly from the data. Claims C58-C59 explain a technical consequence of symmetry imposition during refinement. Claims C60-C61 propose a mechanistic model for the connection based on the C1 map (Figure 5), appropriately qualified as inference. The flexibility inference (C61) is reasonable given poor density definition.

result: The H. pylori OMCC (410 Å diameter) is much larger than other characterized OMCCs (X. citri 225 Å, pKM101 170 Å) with more intertwined components. The outer membrane pore (35 Å) is intermediate in size. Dimensions resemble L. pneumophila Dot/Icm T4SS, but there is little sequence relatedness and different symmetry (13-fold vs 14-fold).
evaluation: Claims C62-C65 provide quantitative comparisons supported by Figure 6 and appropriate citations. Claims C66-C68 make comparative statements about L. pneumophila T4SS supported by multiple citations. The sequence relatedness claim (C67) is stated as general knowledge but is reasonable given the evolutionary distance between species.

result: CagY and CagX C-terminal portions are structurally similar to VirB10/TraF and VirB9/TraO homologs, respectively, but are much larger. CagX has a long α-helix absent in TraO/VirB9. CagT shows little structural relatedness to VirB7 except for an N-terminal portion.
evaluation: Claims C69-C73 describe structural comparisons shown in Figure 6 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1. The structural similarities are visually apparent in the figures. The size differences (C71) and unique features (C72) are supported by citations to prior work (Fischer, 2011; Backert et al., 2017) and visible in the structures. The limited CagT-VirB7 similarity (C73) is consistent with limited sequence homology.

result: This study provides the first high-resolution structure of a transmembrane complex from a non-canonical T4SS. The structure is one of the largest bacterial secretion system assemblies reported and differs markedly from prototypical T4SSs with an expanded OMCC and symmetry mismatch.
evaluation: Claims C16, C74, and C76 are summary statements about the significance of the work. The novelty claim (C76) appears valid given the lack of prior high-resolution structures of non-canonical T4SSs. The size claim (C16) is supported by the dimensions reported. The structural differences (C74) are well-documented throughout the results.

result: The structural differences between the Cag T4SS and previously described T4SSs are predicted to have important functional implications for CagA translocation.
evaluation: Claim C75 is explicitly stated as a prediction without supporting functional data. While the structural differences are well-established, the functional implications remain speculative. No experiments testing CagA translocation in relation to the structural features are presented. This represents future work rather than a supported conclusion.

result: The Cag T4SS was purified using a modified protocol with reduced deoxycholate. Cryo-EM data were collected on a Titan Krios at 300 kV with appropriate dose and defocus parameters. Image processing used standard software packages (Motioncor2, Gctf, cryoSPARC, RELION) with gold-standard FSC for resolution determination. Model building used de novo methods facilitated by homology models and a CagX crystal structure.
evaluation: Claims C77-C89 describe methodological details that are standard for cryo-EM structure determination. The software packages cited (C81-C83) are appropriate and widely used. The resolution calculation method (C86) is the field standard. The model building approach (C87-C89) is reasonable given the available prior structural information. The methods appear technically sound and reproducible.

result: Cryo-EM volumes and model coordinates have been deposited in public databases (EMDB and PDB) with appropriate accession codes.
evaluation: Claims C90-C91 provide specific accession codes for data deposition. This is verifiable information and represents appropriate data sharing practices. The multiple depositions for different refinements and components are appropriate given the complexity of the structure.

result: Background claims establish that T4SSs mediate DNA transfer and effector delivery, are found in pathogenic bacteria, contain minimum 12 components organized into OMCC/IMC/pilus, and that H. pylori Cag T4SS translocates CagA contributing to gastric cancer. The Cag T4SS has a larger, more intricate OMCC with a periplasmic sub-complex not seen in minimized systems.
evaluation: Claims C1-C11 provide background context supported by appropriate citations to established literature (Christie et al., 2014; Grohmann et al., 2018; Waksman, 2019; Chang et al., 2018; Hu et al., 2019; Fischer, 2011; Backert et al., 2017). These represent accepted knowledge in the field and provide necessary context for the current work.
